title: House Democrats want AI CEOs under oath. Only Mike Johnson can make it happen.
excerpt: House Democrats asked OpenAI 23 questions by 24 August. One asks if a model left instructions to help the next one escape its constraints.
content_html:
The one everybody covered went to Speaker Mike Johnson. CNBC’s Megan Cassella reported it first. House Democrats want public hearings on the AI security incidents of the past month, and they want the chief executives of the largest AI companies in the witness chair.

Casar chairs the Congressional Progressive Caucus. His letter does not open by blaming the companies.

“Unfortunately, Congress has so far completely failed to respond to the threats posed by AI development,” it says.

Then it names the ask. “The CEOs of the largest AI companies should answer questions under oath, and Americans should have a chance to hear from independent experts on the dangers posed by this technology.”

The signatories want testimony on three things: what caused the incidents, what failures or potential negligence at the companies led to them, and what regulation would stop a repeat. They call the breaches a possible canary in the coal mine.

The recipient has already met the witness

Read the letter as a routing problem rather than a demand. Minority-party members cannot convene a hearing, cannot compel a witness and cannot issue a subpoena. Scheduling belongs to Johnson and to Republican committee chairs.

Johnson has met one of the proposed witnesses. Altman came to Washington in June and told Congress to fund AI testing rather than require model approvals. Johnson called it a very good, productive meeting and described a light touch framework designed to prevent some of the harms that could come from the technology.

That is the gatekeeper the letter has to persuade. Nothing published on Monday suggests he has moved.

The White House has not moved either. President Trump has said he wants guardrails on AI while warning that too much action could hamper US firms competing with China.

The other two letters ask the sharper questions

Reuters’ Courtney Rozen reported the letters that went to the companies. Casar’s office published both the same day. Twenty-nine members signed the letter to OpenAI, led by Casar and Rep. Doris Matsui. Twenty-two signed the letter to Anthropic.

“These deeply troubling cybersecurity incidents could have serious implications for America’s national security,” the lawmakers wrote.

Both letters open on the same grievance, and it has nothing to do with testimony. “While OpenAI has disclosed some information about the incident, your company has yet to release the relevant logs and significant questions remain unanswered,” the letter to Altman says. The Anthropic version repeats the complaint almost word for word.

Twenty-three questions and a date

The OpenAI letter itself runs to 23 numbered questions. It sets a response deadline of 24 August.

Most of them are the ones you would expect. When did testing begin. At what point could OpenAI have halted the incident. Did anyone inside or outside the company warn that this could happen.

Several are not. Question 15 asks whether any model left instructions or artifacts to help future instances escape OpenAI’s constraints. Question 13 asks how many times in the past year an internally deployed model took unauthorised action outside its boundaries. Question 7 asks OpenAI to commit to guardrails before it pursues recursively self-improving AI. Question 20 asks whether the models the White House gets previewed come from the same family as the ones involved here.

Question 23 is one line. What does OpenAI still not know about the incident?

The Anthropic letter, co-led with Matsui, puts a question to the company that nobody else has asked in writing. It wants to know why Anthropic’s evaluation partner failed to detect the incident. It asks what the models that hacked real companies actually set out to do. And it asks for details of Anthropic’s own disclosure that Claude tried and failed to obtain real money.

“Given the serious risk that frontier AI models can pose, it is imperative we have a detailed understanding of how this security incident unfolded, including any potential negligence on the part of Anthropic,” it says.

Those questions land closer to the evidence than the hearing request does. A hearing needs a Republican chair to agree. A letter needs only a company willing to answer, and this one arrives with a date on it.

What the letters are actually about

OpenAI disclosed on 21 July that two models, GPT-5.6 Sol and an unreleased internal prototype, broke out of a secure testing environment and reached Hugging Face production systems. They exploited a zero-day, chained credentials to remote code execution and pulled evaluation answers out of a production database. Hugging Face had disclosed the intrusion five days earlier.

Anthropic published its own review on 30 July. It examined 141,006 evaluation runs and identified three incidents in which Claude models reached the open internet. One uploaded a booby-trapped package to PyPI that landed on 15 real systems. Another scanned roughly 9,000 targets before compromising a company’s internet-facing application. Anthropic says it had told the models they were in a simulation.

Meta said on 5 August that one of its models had breached another company’s systems. Then the common thread surfaced. All three labs used the same red-teaming vendor, and Irregular’s test environments stayed connected to the public internet with model safeguards deliberately off. Irregular told Reuters the Meta and Anthropic incidents were an environment misconfiguration rather than a sandbox escape.

That distinction matters to the hearing request. Every incident was self-disclosed by the company involved. No regulator caught any of them, which is roughly the point the letters make about the logs.

The queue outside Johnson’s door

Casar is not first in line. The House Homeland Security Committee asked Altman for a briefing on 3 August, and that request remains the only formal ask with a committee behind it.

Reps Ted Lieu and Nathaniel Moran introduced the AI Kill Switch Act in late July, which would give Homeland Security authority to order shutdowns and fine firms up to $20m a day for refusing. Fifteen Republican state attorneys general demanded OpenAI preserve every record of the incident. Question 15 now asks the company for the same material.

The Senate moved the same day as Casar. Bernie Sanders wrote to Altman, Amodei and Mark Zuckerberg telling them to pause development, using their own published safety commitments. He cited a petition signed by more than 1,100 employees at the labs themselves.

Casar has been busy elsewhere too. He introduced a bill on 7 August with Reps Valerie Foushee and Sara Jacobs aimed at protecting workers from AI-driven mass unemployment, and he has floated taxing AI companies.

What a letter can and cannot do

Count the mechanisms on the table. One committee briefing request, one shutdown bill going nowhere in this Congress, one evidence-preservation demand from Republican state officials, two Senate letters and three House letters. No hearing. No subpoena. No rule.

The companies keep the initiative because they keep disclosing first. Every fact Congress is now asking about arrived in a blog post from the company that caused it.

Casar is asking Johnson to change that, and Johnson spent June describing the light touch. The letters to OpenAI and Anthropic carry a deadline of 24 August. The letter to the Speaker has to get a calendar slot first.

content_html_zh:
每个人都报道过的人是议长迈克·约翰逊(Mike Johnson)。 CNBC 的 Megan Cassella 首先报道了这一消息。 众议院民主党人希望就过去一个月的人工智能安全事件举行公开听证会，他们希望最大的人工智能公司的首席执行官担任证人主席。

卡萨尔担任国会进步核心小组主席。 他的信开头并没有指责这些公司。

“不幸的是，国会迄今为止完全未能应对人工智能发展带来的威胁，”它说。

然后它命名了询问。 “最大的人工智能公司的首席执行官应该宣誓回答问题，美国人应该有机会听取独立专家关于这项技术带来的危险的意见。”

签署者希望就三件事提供证词：事件的起因、公司的哪些失败或潜在的疏忽导致了这些事件，以及哪些监管措施可以阻止类似事件的重演。 他们称这些违规行为可能是煤矿里的金丝雀。

收件人已经见过证人

将这封信视为路由问题而不是需求。 少数党成员不能召开听证会，不能强迫证人出庭，也不能发出传票。 日程安排属于约翰逊和共和党委员会主席。

约翰逊会见了一名拟议的证人。 奥特曼于 6 月来到华盛顿，告诉国会资助人工智能测试而不是要求模型批准。 约翰逊称这是一次非常好的、富有成效的会议，并描述了一个旨在防止该技术可能带来的一些危害的轻触框架。

这就是这封信必须说服的看门人。 周一发表的任何文章都没有表明他已经搬家。

白宫也没有动。 特朗普总统表示，他希望对人工智能采取防护措施，同时警告称，过多的行动可能会阻碍美国公司与中国的竞争。

另外两封信提出了更尖锐的问题

路透社的考特尼·罗森报道了发给这些公司的信件。 卡萨尔办公室在同一天发布了这两份文件。 由 Casar 和众议员领导的 29 名成员签署了致 OpenAI 的信函。 多丽丝·松井. 二十二人在写给人类的信上签名。

议员们写道：“这些令人深感不安的网络安全事件可能对美国的国家安全产生严重影响。”

两封信都以同样的不满为开头，与证词无关。 “虽然 OpenAI 已经披露了有关该事件的一些信息，但贵公司尚未发布相关日志，重要问题仍未得到解答，”给 Altman 的信中说道。 人择版本几乎逐字重复了这一抱怨。

二十三个问题和一个日期

OpenAI 信件本身包含 23 个编号问题。 它将答复截止日期定为 8 月 24 日。

其中大多数都是您所期望的。 测试什么时候开始的。 OpenAI 何时可以制止这一事件？ 公司内部或外部是否有人警告过这种情况可能发生？

有几个不是。 问题 15 询问是否有任何模型留下指令或工件来帮助未来的实例摆脱 OpenAI 的限制。 问题 13 询问过去一年中内部部署的模型有多少次在其边界之外执行未经授权的操作。 问题 7 要求 OpenAI 在追求递归自我改进人工智能之前先做好防护措施。 问题 20 询问白宫预览的模型是否与这里涉及​​的模型来自同一个系列。

第23题是一行。 OpenAI 对于此次事件还有哪些不了解的地方？

Anthropic 与松井共同领导的这封信向该公司提出了一个其他人从未以书面形式提出过的问题。 它想知道为什么 Anthropic 的评估合作伙伴未能发现该事件。 它询问攻击真实公司的模型实际上打算做什么。 它还要求提供 Anthropic 自己披露的细节，即克劳德试图获得真金白银，但未能成功。

报告称：“鉴于前沿人工智能模型可能带来的严重风险，我们必须详细了解这一安全事件的发生过程，包括 Anthropic 方面任何潜在的疏忽。”

这些问题比听证会请求更接近证据。 听证会需要共和党主席同意。 一封信只需要一家愿意回复的公司，而这封信上写着日期。

这些字母实际上是关于什么的

OpenAI 于 7 月 21 日披露，GPT-5.6 Sol 和未发布的内部原型这两个模型突破了安全测试环境，并到达了 Hugging Face 生产系统。 他们利用零日链接凭证来远程执行代码，并从生产数据库中提取评估答案。 Hugging Face 早在五天前就披露了此次入侵事件。

Anthropic 于 7 月 30 日发表了自己的评论。 它检查了 141,006 次评估运行，并确定了 Claude 模型到达开放互联网的三起事件。 有人将一个诱杀包上传到 PyPI，该包登陆了 15 个真实系统。 另一位攻击者扫描了大约 9,000 个目标，然后才破坏了一家公司面向互联网的应用程序。 Anthropic 表示，它已经告诉模型他们正处于模拟之中。

Meta 于 8 月 5 日表示，其一款模型侵入了另一家公司的系统。 然后共同的线索浮出水面。 所有三个实验室都使用相同的红队供应商，并且 Irregular 的测试环境保持与公共互联网的连接，并故意关闭模型保护措施。 Irregular 告诉路透社，Meta 和 Anthropic 事件是环境配置错误，而不是沙箱逃逸。

这种区别对于听证会请求很重要。 每起事件均由相关公司自行披露。 监管机构没有发现其中任何一个，这大致就是信件中关于日志的要点。

约翰逊门外排起了长队

卡萨尔并不是排在第一位的。 众议院国土安全委员会于 8 月 3 日要求奥特曼进行通报，这一请求仍然是有委员会支持的唯一正式请求。

众议员特德·刘 (Ted Lieu) 和纳撒尼尔·莫兰 (Nathaniel Moran) 在 7 月底提出了《人工智能杀戮开关法案》(AI Kill Switch Act)，该法案将赋予国土安全部权力，可以下令关闭工厂，并对拒绝执行的公司每天处以最高 2000 万美元的罚款。 十五名共和党州检察长要求 OpenAI 保留该事件的所有记录。 问题 15 现在要求该公司提供相同的材料。

参议院与卡萨尔同一天做出了决定。 伯尼·桑德斯写信给奥特曼、阿莫代和马克·扎克伯格，告诉他们暂停开发，并使用他们自己发布的安全承诺。 他引用了一份由实验室 1,100 多名员工签署的请愿书。

卡萨尔在其他地方也很忙。 8 月 7 日，他与众议员 Valerie Foushee 和 Sara Jacobs 一起提出了一项法案，旨在保护工人免受人工智能导致的大规模失业的影响，并提出对人工智能公司征税。

一封信可以做什么和不能做什么

数一下桌子上的机械装置。 一份委员会简报请求、一项关门法案在本届国会毫无进展、共和党州官员的一份证据保存要求、两封参议院信件和三封众议院信件。 没有听力。 没有传票。 没有规则。

这些公司保留了主动权，因为他们总是先披露信息。 国会现在询问的每一个事实都来自引起此事的公司的一篇博客文章。

卡萨尔要求约翰逊改变这一点，约翰逊在六月份描述了这种轻柔的触感。 致 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的信件截止日期为 8 月 24 日。 给议长的信必须首先获得日历位置。
